title: Plan secure firmware updates after launch, including UK connected-device security law (PSTI)
summary: Connected devices need security updates for years. In the UK, consumer connected products must meet baseline security rules, including how long you will provide updates.

beginner: Check whether your product connects to the internet or a home network.
Read the UK rules for consumer connectable products (the PSTI regime).
Make sure there are no default passwords shared across devices.
Publish how people can report security issues.
Decide and publish how long you will provide security updates.
intermediate: Plan secure over-the-air updates, including how to recover from a failed update.
Prepare the statement of compliance with your legal team.
Agree how quickly security fixes ship after a report.
experienced: Set an update and support-period policy across devices.
Budget for updates over the whole support period.
Track related rules in other markets, such as the EU Cyber Resilience Act.

toolExamples.github: Keep firmware release notes with each tagged release.
toolExamples.confluence: Publish the security reporting page and support period.

pitfalls: Treating launch as the end of the work
No way to recover a device after a failed update
A support period nobody has budgeted for

sources.title: The UK Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure (Product Security) regime (GOV.UK)
